prompt:
Scene:
A square color magazine advertisement page in the style of 1961 American kitchenware print ads. Full product-hero layout: appliance centered on a gradient studio backdrop, headline banner at top, small tagline banner at bottom. Halftone print grain, slight CMYK offset, matte coated-paper feel.

Subject:
An imaginary atomic-age bubble-top percolator coffee maker: an ivory enamel base with chrome handle, a tall chrome column, and a clear glass bubble at the top where rich brown coffee is bubbling and splashing visibly. A red bakelite switch on the side. Below the coffee maker a single cadmium-red ceramic cup and saucer sits steaming, with a pink sugar cube beside it. Backdrop is a soft yellow-to-turquoise gradient. Stylized starburst motifs decorate the top corners.

Important details:
Strict atomic-age palette: ivory, turquoise, cadmium red, bright yellow, powder pink, chrome. Appliance form must read as what 1961 imagined a futuristic percolator would look like: chrome column, glass bubble, analog switch, bulbous proportions. Rendering must feel like printed illustration, not photo: halftone grain, flat highlights, slight sketch-style chrome outlines.

Use case:
Atomic Appliance Studies single study 5 of 5, independent product ad mockup.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, no modern espresso machine, no LCD display, no touchscreen, no photoreal depth-of-field, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio.
